samples.title: Bit ribbons: Proof strip
samples.statement:
A punch ribbon stores its active holes as the set bits of a nonnegative reading. Rafi rolls a fresh proof strip into the office typewriter. The supervisor wants the readings in their precise working order before signing the file.

For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0.

Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.

Implement bitRibbonsProofStrip(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

samples.title: Bit ribbons: Peak ticket
samples.statement:
A punch ribbon stores its active holes as the set bits of a nonnegative reading. Ada is setting the upper stop on an old office gauge. The largest derived reading goes on its label, even if the whole tray is below zero.

For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0.

Return the largest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. Negative maxima must remain negative.

Implement bitRibbonsPeakTicket(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

samples.title: Bit ribbons: Boss receipt
samples.statement:
A punch ribbon stores its active holes as the set bits of a nonnegative reading. Neri adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

For each nonnegative reading, produce the number of 1 bits in its binary representation. The reading 0 contributes 0.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement bitRibbonsBossReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
